instanceNetwork.title: Public IP
instanceNetwork.descriptionBefore: The addresses this server is reachable at from the internet. The IPv4 anchors the
instanceNetwork.descriptionAfter: fallback domains every resource gets before you own a real domain, and it's what Cloudflare auto-configure points A records at. IPv6 is optional — plenty of hosts have none. Auto-detected on first boot in production. Correct them here if detection got it wrong (NAT, multi-homed host).
instanceNetwork.pinnedBy: Pinned by {{vars}}, which re-applies on every boot, so edits here wouldn't stick. Change or unset it to manage from this page.
instanceNetwork.certSelfSigned: Verified, but the edge is still serving a self-signed certificate ({{issuer}}), so browsers will refuse this domain.
instanceNetwork.certMissing: Verified, but the edge has no certificate for this domain yet, so https:// cannot load.
instanceNetwork.certBlockedHint: Let's Encrypt validates over inbound port 80. Check that ports 80 and 443 reach this server from the internet — a cloud firewall or security group blocking them is the usual cause, and it is invisible from inside the machine.
instanceNetwork.certExpired: Verified, but the certificate the edge serves for this domain has expired, so browsers will refuse it.

welcome.title: A quick tour
welcome.description: Six minutes through the parts of otterdeploy you'll use daily: where your machines live, how a project is laid out, and where to look when a deploy goes wrong. Leave any time with Esc; it's in your account menu when you want it back.

sidebar.title: The sidebar
sidebar.description: Everything org-wide lives here, grouped by what it's for: your projects at the top, the infrastructure they run on in the middle, and the outbound connections a deploy needs (git, registries, keys) below that.

projects.title: Projects
projects.description: A project groups the services, databases, and routes that ship together: one app and its dependencies. The badge counts what this workspace has.

infrastructure.title: Servers
infrastructure.description: The Linux machines in your swarm. Add one over SSH or with a join token, then watch its role, availability, and health from the table. Nothing deploys until at least one node is ready.

edge.title: Edge
edge.description: The Caddy layer in front of everything you deploy: domains and routes, TLS certificates, access logs, and the host firewall. This is where you go when a URL doesn't resolve or a certificate hasn't issued.

search.title: Search anything
search.description: The command palette jumps to any page, project, or resource without leaving the keyboard. Press ⌘K from anywhere.

activity.title: Live system state
activity.description: Running deploys, unread notifications, and the theme switch. The mark in the top-left changes with the same state, so a build in progress is visible from any page, and from a background tab.

serversPage.title: Your cluster
serversPage.description: One row per machine, with its swarm role, availability, and last health sample. `unknown` is deliberately not a pass: it means nobody has checked yet.

addServer.title: Add a server
addServer.description: Provision over SSH and otterdeploy walks the whole path itself: install Docker, join the mesh, join the swarm, verify the node, label it for builds. Each phase reports honestly as it runs.

enrollment.title: Or enrol without SSH
enrollment.description: Prefer not to hand over SSH? Generate a short-lived join token and run one command on the machine instead. Useful for hosts you can only reach from a console.

projectGraph.title: The project graph
projectGraph.description: Your project as a canvas: services, databases, and the routes that reach them, with live status on every node. Right-click a node to open, restart, clone, or read its logs; right-click the canvas to add something new.

projectTabs.title: Everything about this project
projectTabs.description: The graph is the overview; these tabs are the detail. Deployments, logs, metrics, variables, and networking all stay scoped to this project.

newService.title: Add a service
newService.description: Build from a git repo, pull a Docker image, launch a database, or paste a compose file. The fast path is three or four clicks; "Advanced setup" opens the full flow when you need it.

deployments.title: Every deploy, kept
deployments.description: One row per push, with its reason (git-push, redeploy, env-change, rollback) and the config snapshot it ran with. That snapshot is what makes rolling back a real option rather than a guess.

logs.title: Logs that tell the truth
logs.description: Runtime logs from your containers and edge logs from Caddy, in one place. Filter by service, level, and time; every filter lives in the URL, so a useful view is a link you can send someone.

variables.title: Variables
variables.description: Set them per project or per service, and reference other resources by name: `${database:main.DATABASE_URL}` resolves at deploy time. That late binding is what lets previews get their own database without editing config.

networking.title: Domains and routes
networking.description: Point a domain at a service and otterdeploy handles DNS checks and certificate issuance, reporting each state plainly. Deployment protection can put an auth wall in front of anything not ready to be public.

help.title: Where this lives
help.description: The tour is here whenever you want it again, next to the command menu and your account settings.

done.title: That's the shape of it
done.description: The rest is documentation and the command palette. If something looks wrong, the honest answer is usually on the Deployments or Logs tab; otterdeploy tries never to hide a failure behind a spinner.

commandPalette.title: Command palette
commandPalette.description: Search for a command to run…

organization.title: Create your organization
organization.description: An organization is your top-level workspace: it owns your projects, servers, domains, and team. You can create more later or invite people in.

domain.title: Set a base domain
domain.description: Where your deployed apps and databases get their public URLs, not the dashboard itself.
domain.label: Base domain

project.title: Create your first project
project.description: A project groups the services, databases, and routes that ship together, like one app and its dependencies. We'll drop you straight into it.

updates.bannerAvailable: A new version of otterdeploy is available
updates.dryRunHint: Dev/dry-run install. Applying runs as a simulation.
updates.descriptionDryRun: Dry-run mode: this simulates the full update and streams progress, but changes nothing. No images are pulled and the control plane will not restart.
updates.descriptionReal: This pulls the new images and restarts the control plane. The dashboard will be briefly unavailable and this page will reconnect automatically when it's back.
updates.reasonAlreadyRunning: An update is already in progress.
updates.reasonNoUpdate: You're already on the latest version.
updates.reasonDowngrade: The available version isn't newer than what's running.
updates.dryDone: Simulated update complete. No containers were changed.
updates.waitingCutover: Waiting for the control plane to come back on {{target}}. This page will reload automatically.
updates.applying: Applying the update. The control plane will restart and this page will reconnect automatically.
updates.resetOk: Update reset. You can start it again.
updates.runningSubReal: The dashboard will go away briefly and reconnect on {{target}}. That's normal.
updates.runningSubDry: Simulation only. No containers will be changed.
updates.cutoverReload: This page reloads automatically the moment the new version answers.
updates.stuckHint: Still no answer after {{count}} probes. If the update helper died, reset and start again.
updates.slowHint: This is taking longer than expected.
updates.closeBlocked: The update keeps running. This dialog can't be closed until it finishes.

registries.label: Registry

ghcr.description: Covered by your GitHub App. Pushes and pulls are authorized per request, so there is nothing here to create or rotate.
ghcr.descriptionAs: Covered by your GitHub App, installed on {{account}}. Pushes and pulls are authorized per request, so there is nothing here to create or rotate.
ghcr.needsPermission: Your GitHub App needs access to packages before this works. GitHub asks an owner to approve the change — it is not granted automatically.
ghcr.nothingToRotate: Authorized per request — nothing to rotate

registries.noteUsed: Used by the builder (docker push) and the swarm daemon (docker pull).
registries.noteUnused: No project pushes here yet. Name it as a service's image target to start using it.
registries.removeBody: {{count}} project(s) push to {{host}} through this credential. Their builds will fail until a new one is wired up.
registries.removeBodyUnused: Nothing currently pushes to {{host}}, so removing this affects no builds.

sso.providerIdHint: Appears in the redirect URI you give your IdP. Cannot be changed later.
sso.clientSecretHint: Stored encrypted and never shown again. To rotate it, remove the provider and add it back.
sso.deriveHint: Leave blank to derive it from the issuer.
sso.instanceDisabled: Enterprise SSO is switched off for this installation, so these providers do not appear on the sign-in page and cannot sign anyone in. An install administrator can turn it back on in Settings → Instance → Sign-in methods. Providers registered here are kept either way.
sso.methodsDescription: How people prove who they are on this installation. The sign-in page shows exactly what is enabled here.
sso.passwordOn: On. People sign in with an email address and a password, and can reset it by email.
sso.passwordLockedBootstrap: The first account has to be created with a password and the installer's bootstrap token, so this stays on until someone signs up.
sso.passwordLockedNoFederated: Nothing else can sign anyone in yet. Configure a social provider below, or register an identity provider in Workspace → SSO, before turning passwords off.
sso.passkeyDescription: Passwordless sign-in with a device biometric or a security key. Off also stops anyone registering a new passkey; existing ones are kept, not deleted, and start working again if you turn this back on.
sso.enterpriseNoProviders: No identity provider is registered yet. Add one in Workspace → SSO; this switch controls whether its button appears on the sign-in page.
sso.enterpriseDescription: Per-workspace OIDC identity providers (Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace, Authentik). Each registered provider gets its own button on the sign-in page. Turning this off leaves the providers configured but stops them signing anyone in.

firewall.alreadyBanned: This IP already has an active CrowdSec ban.
firewall.blockAria: Block an IP or CIDR range
firewall.yourListsSubtitle: Public + custom lists imported into CrowdSec on a schedule.
firewall.publicListsSubtitle: Well-known free lists, no CrowdSec account needed. One click to add.
firewall.removeListDescription: The list and every IP it imported are dropped from the firewall. You can re-add it from the catalog or by URL later.

activepieces.description: No-code automation with 200+ integrations and a branching flow builder: the open alternative to Zapier. Postgres for flow state, Redis for the job queue.

env.AP_FRONTEND_URL: Public base URL. Webhook endpoints and OAuth callbacks are built from it.
env.AP_ENCRYPTION_KEY: 32-character hex key encrypting stored connection credentials.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres.

anythingllm.description: All-in-one RAG workspace. Drop in documents, pick a model, and chat over them with citations. Bundles its own vector store, so there is nothing else to run.

env.JWT_SECRET: Signs session tokens for the multi-user mode.

appsmith.description: Drag-and-drop internal tools over your existing databases and APIs, with JavaScript anywhere a value goes. The community image bundles its own database, cache and object store.

env.APPSMITH_ENCRYPTION_PASSWORD: Encrypts the datasource credentials Appsmith stores. Change it after first boot and every saved connection becomes unreadable.
env.APPSMITH_ENCRYPTION_SALT: Salt paired with the password above. Same warning applies.

authentik.description: Self-hosted identity provider: SSO, OAuth2/OIDC, SAML, and LDAP with a policy engine. Server and worker share a bundled Postgres and Redis; both persist to named volumes.

env.SECRET_KEY: Signing key for sessions and tokens. Keep it stable across restarts.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled authentik Postgres.

autumn.description: Open-source pricing and billing layer over Stripe: model products and features once, then meter usage and gate access with attach / check / track calls. Runs the API server, queue workers, cron, and dashboard from one prebuilt image, with bundled Postgres, Valkey, Dragonfly and a DynamoDB emulator. Stripe keys are added per-org in the dashboard after deploy.

env.AUTUMN_API_URL: Public origin the API server is exposed on (scheme + host only, no path). Expose the `server` service and use that URL.
env.CLIENT_URL: Public origin the dashboard is exposed on. Expose the `dashboard` service and use that URL.
env.ENCRYPTION_IV: Hex IV for encrypting stored Stripe keys.
env.ENCRYPTION_PASSWORD: Key material for encrypting stored Stripe keys.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres.

baserow.description: Spreadsheet-shaped database with a REST API: an open-source Airtable. Single image bundling web, API and worker; data and uploads persist to one named volume.

env.BASEROW_PUBLIC_URL: Public base URL. The frontend calls the API at this address.

beszel.description: Lightweight monitoring hub: CPU, memory, disk, network and per-container stats, with history and alerts, in one small Go binary. The hub only displays data. Each machine you want charted runs a Beszel agent, and the hub hands you its install command when you add the system.

env.APP_URL: Public base URL of the hub. Used in alert emails and OAuth redirects.

bookstack.description: Documentation organised the way a library is — shelves, books, chapters, pages — with WYSIWYG or Markdown editing and full-text search.

env.BOOKSTACK_URL: The full URL BookStack is served at, scheme included. A mismatch breaks the login POST.
env.APP_KEY: Laravel encryption key, and it must keep the `base64:` prefix. BookStack encrypts stored third-party credentials with it, so replacing it later leaves those unreadable.

browserless.description: Headless Chrome as a service. Point Puppeteer or Playwright at it over websocket for screenshots, PDFs and scraping, without shipping a browser inside your own image.

env.BROWSERLESS_TOKEN: Bearer token every connecting client must present.

budibase.description: Build and self-host business apps from data you already have, with a form and table builder and a built-in database. One container carrying its own CouchDB, Redis and object store.

env.INTERNAL_API_KEY: Authenticates the bundled services to each other.
env.MINIO_ACCESS_KEY: Access key for the built-in object store that holds uploads and app bundles.
env.MINIO_SECRET_KEY: Secret key matching the access key above.
env.COUCHDB_PASSWORD: Password for the built-in CouchDB, where app definitions and rows live. Changing it after first boot orphans the data behind it.

cal-com.description: Self-hosted scheduling pages: availability, booking links, and calendar sync without handing your calendar to a SaaS.

env.CALCOM_URL: The public URL your booking pages live at. Cal.com bakes it into every booking link it generates.
env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY: Encrypts the calendar and video-provider credentials stored in the database. Losing it means reconnecting every integration.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres.

chatwoot.description: Shared inbox for customer conversations across email, live chat, and social channels, with a built-in AI assistant.

env.FRONTEND_URL: The URL agents and the chat widget reach this install at. Chatwoot signs asset and callback URLs with it.
env.SECRET_KEY_BASE: Rails signing key for sessions and cookies. Changing it later signs everyone out.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled pgvector Postgres.
env.REDIS_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Redis, which holds the Sidekiq job queue.

clickhouse.description: Column-store SQL database for analytics at scale: billions of rows scanned per second on a single node. Native protocol on 9000, HTTP on 8123.

env.CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD: Password for the `clickhouse` user this stack creates. That user gets access management, so it can create further users and grants.

cloudbeaver.description: DBeaver in the browser: a full SQL console with schema navigation, ER diagrams and query history across Postgres, MySQL, SQLite and more, shared by a team.

code-server.description: VS Code running on the server, reached from a browser tab. The editor keeps its extensions and terminal on the machine, so a laptop or tablet is only a screen.

env.CODE_SERVER_PASSWORD: Password for the web UI. Anyone with it gets a shell on this container.

directus.description: Headless CMS and instant REST/GraphQL API over a Postgres database, with an admin app for editors. Uploads persist to a named volume.

env.ADMIN_EMAIL: Email for the first admin user.
env.ADMIN_PASSWORD: Password for the first admin user.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the directus Postgres user.

docker-registry.description: The reference OCI registry: a private place to push images your services then pull. Pairs with a service's image target so builds never leave your own infrastructure.

docmost.description: Collaborative wiki and documentation with real-time editing, spaces and permissions: a self-hosted alternative to Confluence or Notion. Postgres for content, Redis for presence.

env.APP_URL: Public base URL. Used for share links and invite emails.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres.

dozzle.description: Live log viewer for every container on the host. Tail, search and follow without SSH. Reads the Docker socket, so anyone who reaches it can read every container's logs: keep it behind Require login in the service's Deployment protection.

drizzle-gateway.description: Self-hosted Drizzle Studio. Browse and edit any Postgres, MySQL or SQLite database in the browser, with the schema rendered the way Drizzle sees it.

env.GATEWAY_MASTERPASS: Master password guarding the studio and its saved connections.

excalidraw.description: Virtual whiteboard with a hand-drawn feel. A single stateless container serving the editor. Boards live in the browser unless exported.

flowise.description: Drag-and-drop builder for LLM chains and agents. Wire up prompts, tools, retrievers and memory on a canvas, then call the result as an API. Flows persist to a named volume.

env.FLOWISE_PASSWORD: Password for the built-in admin login.

forgejo.description: The community fork of Gitea: a self-hosted Git forge with issues, pull requests and a package registry. Repositories live on a named volume, metadata in a bundled Postgres.

env.FORGEJO_URL: Public base URL. Used for clone URLs and webhook callbacks.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres.

ghost.description: Publishing platform for newsletters, memberships, and a clean editor. Runs the official Ghost image backed by MySQL 8 with persistent content and database volumes.

env.GHOST_URL: Public URL the site is served from (used in links and redirects).
env.MYSQL_PASSWORD: Password for the ghost MySQL user.

gitea.description: Self-hosted Git service: repos, issues, pull requests, and CI runners. Backed by Postgres; repositories persist to a named volume.

env.ROOT_URL: Public URL Gitea is served from (clone URLs, webhooks, OAuth).
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the gitea Postgres user.

glitchtip.description: Error tracking that speaks the Sentry protocol. Point any Sentry SDK at it by changing the DSN. Web and worker share a bundled Postgres and Redis; uploads persist to a volume.

env.GLITCHTIP_DOMAIN: Public base URL. Used in DSNs and links inside notification emails.
env.SECRET_KEY: Django secret. Signs sessions and tokens.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres.

gotenberg.description: Stateless HTTP API that turns HTML, Markdown or Office documents into PDFs. Chromium and LibreOffice live in the container so your app never has to.

grafana-prometheus.description: The canonical metrics stack: Prometheus scrapes and stores time series, Grafana dashboards them. Add scrape targets via Prometheus config after deploy.

env.GF_ADMIN_PASSWORD: Password for the Grafana admin user.

grist.description: Spreadsheets with a real relational model underneath: typed columns, references between tables, and Python formulas. Runs in single-team mode with sign-in required.

env.GRIST_URL: The URL Grist is served at. Share links and the login redirect are built from it.
env.GRIST_DEFAULT_EMAIL: The email address that owns this installation. Whoever signs in with it becomes the owner, so use an address you control.

hasura.description: Instant GraphQL over Postgres. Introspects the schema and serves queries, mutations and subscriptions with row-level permissions, no resolvers to write.

env.HASURA_ADMIN_SECRET: Admin secret for the console and unrestricted API access.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres that Hasura exposes.

healthchecks.description: Dead-man's-switch monitoring for cron jobs and backups. Each job pings a URL when it finishes, and you get alerted when a ping does not arrive on schedule.

env.SITE_ROOT: Public base URL. Appears in ping URLs and alert emails.
env.SECRET_KEY: Django secret. Signs sessions and tokens.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres.

home-assistant.description: Local-first home automation: devices, scenes and automations evaluated on your own server rather than a vendor cloud. Runs in bridge networking, so add devices by address or via MQTT rather than relying on broadcast discovery.

hoppscotch.description: API client in the browser: REST, GraphQL and WebSocket requests with collections and environments. A self-hosted alternative to Postman that never syncs your tokens anywhere.

immich.description: Self-hosted photo and video backup with mobile apps, face and object recognition, and timeline browsing. The machine-learning service runs alongside, so nothing is sent off the box.

env.DB_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres. Immich needs the vector-enabled build shipped here, not stock Postgres.

infisical.description: Secrets manager with per-environment values, versioning and audit logs, plus CLI and SDK access. Bundled Postgres for secrets and Redis for sessions and queues.

env.SITE_URL: Public base URL. Used for invite links and OAuth callbacks.
env.ENCRYPTION_KEY: Encrypts every stored secret at rest. Losing it makes them unrecoverable.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres.

it-tools.description: The utility drawer: hash and JWT decoders, UUID and password generators, cron parsers, base64, regex testers, colour converters. Everything runs client-side once loaded.

jaeger.description: Distributed tracing. Send OpenTelemetry spans and follow one request across every service it touched. All-in-one image with in-memory storage, so it starts with no dependencies.

jellyfin.description: Media server for movies, shows and music, with clients on most TVs and phones. No accounts, no tracking, no paid tier.

env.JELLYFIN_URL: The URL clients reach this server at. Jellyfin advertises it to apps that discover the server automatically.

jitsi.description: Video meetings with no accounts and no plugins. Runs the whole Jitsi stack: the web app, the XMPP server, the conference focus, and the media bridge.

env.JITSI_PUBLIC_URL: The URL participants join meetings at. Jitsi puts it in invitations and treats it as the browser origin.
env.JVB_ADVERTISE_IP: The public IP address participants can reach this server on. Media flows over UDP straight to the bridge, so the bridge has to advertise an address that works from outside — a private IP here means everyone connects and nobody hears anything.
env.JICOFO_AUTH_PASSWORD: Password for the `focus` XMPP account. Prosody creates the account with it and Jicofo signs in with it, so both sides read the same value.
env.JICOFO_COMPONENT_SECRET: Shared secret between Jicofo and Prosody's component port.
env.JVB_AUTH_PASSWORD: Password for the `jvb` XMPP account the media bridge signs in with.

karakeep.description: Save links, notes and images and let AI tag them for you. The headless-Chrome sidecar archives a readable copy and a screenshot of every page.

env.KARAKEEP_URL: The URL you open Karakeep at. Used as the auth callback origin, so browser extensions and the mobile app both depend on it being right.
env.MEILI_MASTER_KEY: Shared key between Karakeep and its Meilisearch index. The same value is set on both sides.

kestra.description: Declarative orchestration for data, AI and infrastructure workflows, written as YAML and versioned. Postgres backs both the repository and the queue.

env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres. It appears in Kestra's own YAML configuration as well as on the database.

keycloak.description: Identity provider with OIDC and SAML, user federation, social login and fine-grained authorization. The standard choice when something downstream expects real SSO.

env.KEYCLOAK_HOSTNAME: Public hostname Keycloak issues tokens for. It must match how users reach it.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres that stores realms and users.

librechat.description: One chat interface for every model you have a key for — Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, or anything OpenAI-compatible, including your own Ollama or LiteLLM stack. Conversations in MongoDB, search via Meilisearch.

env.LIBRECHAT_URL: The URL LibreChat is served at, used as both the client and server origin.
env.CREDS_KEY: Encrypts the per-user provider API keys stored in the database. Exactly 32 bytes of hex.
env.CREDS_IV: Initialisation vector paired with the key above. Exactly 16 bytes of hex.
env.JWT_REFRESH_SECRET: Signs the refresh tokens. Keep it distinct from the access secret.
env.MEILI_MASTER_KEY: Shared key between LibreChat and its Meilisearch index.

libretranslate.description: Self-hosted machine translation API, with no per-character billing and no text leaving your server. Downloads language models on first start into a named volume.

listmonk.description: Newsletter and mailing-list manager: subscriber lists, segmentation, campaign templates and bounce handling, driven by your own SMTP. Single binary plus Postgres.

env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres that stores subscribers and campaigns.

litellm.description: One OpenAI-compatible endpoint in front of every LLM provider: routing, budgets, keys and spend tracking. Backed by its own Postgres for keys and usage records.

env.LITELLM_MASTER_KEY: Admin key for the proxy. It issues and revokes every other virtual key.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres that stores keys and spend.

livekit.description: The real-time media server behind live video, voice and AI agent apps: rooms, tracks and WebRTC routing, with a Redis coordinator. Runs all participant media on one UDP port so it works without host networking.

env.LIVEKIT_API_KEY: Identifier your application signs access tokens with. Not a secret on its own — it travels in every token — but it has to match on both sides.
env.LIVEKIT_API_SECRET: The signing secret paired with the key above. Anything holding it can mint a token for any room, so it belongs on your server and never in a browser bundle.

mailpit.description: SMTP server that captures mail instead of delivering it, with a web inbox to read it. Point a staging app's SMTP at it and nothing can reach a real customer by accident.

matomo.description: Full-featured web analytics you host yourself: sessions, funnels, goals and heatmaps, with raw data that never leaves your server. Heavier than Plausible, and far more detailed.

env.MYSQL_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled MariaDB user Matomo connects as.
env.MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: Root password for the bundled MariaDB.

mattermost.description: Team chat with channels, threads, and calls, on infrastructure you run. Postgres-backed, with config, data, logs and plugins each on their own volume.

env.MATTERMOST_URL: The full URL people will open Mattermost at, scheme included. Mattermost builds its links and CORS rules from this, so a mismatch breaks sign-in.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres. Used by both the database and the connection string.

mautic.description: Marketing automation you host yourself: contacts, segments, campaigns, landing pages and email, with the cron workers that actually drive them enabled.

env.MAUTIC_URL: The full URL Mautic is served at. Tracking pixels and email links are built from it.

meilisearch.description: Lightning-fast, typo-tolerant search engine with a simple REST API. A single service on port 7700; the index persists to a named volume.

env.MEILI_MASTER_KEY: Master key protecting the API. At least 16 bytes.

memos.description: A lightweight, self-hosted timeline for quick notes, logs and snippets. Everything lives in one SQLite file on its volume, and the first account to sign up becomes the host.

metabase.description: Open-source BI: dashboards, questions, and SQL over your existing databases. Application state lives in a dedicated Postgres.

env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the metabase Postgres user.

minio.description: S3-compatible object storage. Exposes the S3 API on 9000 and the web console on 9001; buckets persist to a named volume.

env.MINIO_ROOT_USER: Root access key (username). At least 3 characters.
env.MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: Root secret key. At least 8 characters.

mosquitto.description: The reference MQTT broker: tiny, fast, and what most IoT and device fleets speak. Persists retained messages and subscriptions to a named volume.

n8n.description: Fair-code workflow automation with 400+ integrations. Single service; workflows and credentials persist to a named volume (SQLite).

env.N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY: Encrypts stored credentials. Losing it locks you out of them.
env.WEBHOOK_URL: Public base URL used when registering webhooks with external services.

nats.description: Messaging for services: pub/sub, request/reply and JetStream persistence in one small Go binary. A lighter answer than Kafka when you want a queue, not a log platform.

netbird.description: WireGuard-based private network control plane: management, signal, relay and STUN in one container, with an embedded Dex identity provider so it needs no external IdP. Point otterdeploy's private networking at it to keep services off the public internet.

env.NETBIRD_DOMAIN: Public base URL of this install, scheme included (https://vpn.example.com). Peers and the dashboard's auth redirects are pinned to it, so changing it later re-enrols every peer.
env.NETBIRD_AUTH_SECRET: Shared secret the relay authenticates peers with.
env.NETBIRD_STORE_ENCRYPTION_KEY: Encrypts peer records at rest. Unique per install, and losing it makes the store unreadable.

nextcloud.description: Files, calendars, contacts and collaborative editing on your own server. Postgres for metadata, Redis for file locking, and the app tree on a volume so apps survive upgrades.

env.NEXTCLOUD_TRUSTED_DOMAIN: The hostname Nextcloud will answer on. Requests arriving under any other name are refused, which is the point — it is what stops host-header spoofing.
env.NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_USER: Username for the administrator account created on first boot.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres.

nocobase.description: A no-code platform built around a real data model rather than spreadsheets: define collections, then compose pages, blocks and workflows over them.

env.APP_KEY: Signs sessions and encrypts stored secrets. Replacing it signs everyone out.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres.

nocodb.description: Airtable-style smart spreadsheet over a real database. Runs the official image with a dedicated Postgres for its metadata and data.

env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the nocodb Postgres user.
env.NC_AUTH_JWT_SECRET: Signing secret for NocoDB auth tokens.

ntfy.description: Pub-sub notifications over plain HTTP. Curl a topic and your phone buzzes. No account or SDK needed, which makes it the shortest path from a cron job or alert to a human.

env.NTFY_BASE_URL: Public base URL. Clients subscribe against it, and it appears in links.

odoo.description: The open-source business suite: CRM, sales, inventory, accounting, HR and a website builder, all sharing one database. Install only the apps you need from the UI.

env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres. Odoo creates its own databases at first run, so this account owns the cluster rather than a single database.

open-webui.description: Self-hosted chat UI over a local Ollama runtime. Models, prompts and history stay on your server. Pulls models on demand into a named volume; no external API key needed.

env.WEBUI_SECRET_KEY: Signs session cookies. Changing it logs everyone out.

outline.description: Fast team wiki with real-time editing, full-text search, and Slack-style organisation. Documents live in Postgres; attachments land on a local volume.

env.OUTLINE_URL: The URL the wiki is served at. Outline uses it for share links and the OIDC redirect.
env.SECRET_KEY: Signs sessions and encrypts stored integration credentials. Replacing it invalidates both.
env.UTILS_SECRET: Separate secret guarding the internal maintenance endpoints.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres.
env.OIDC_CLIENT_ID: Client ID from your identity provider. Outline has no local password login, so an OIDC provider is required, not optional.
env.OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET: Client secret matching the ID above.
env.OIDC_USERINFO_URI: Your provider's userinfo endpoint, which is where Outline reads the account's name and email.

paperless-ngx.description: Scan, index and search your paper archive. OCR on ingest, full-text search, and automatic tagging — with Gotenberg and Tika alongside so office documents and email are indexed too.

env.PAPERLESS_URL: The URL Paperless is served at. It has to match, or the login form's CSRF check rejects every attempt.
env.PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY: Django signing key for sessions and CSRF tokens.
env.PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER: Username for the superuser created on first boot.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres.

penpot.description: Open-source design and prototyping for product teams, working in real SVG and CSS so what designers hand over is what developers get. Runs the frontend, backend, export worker, Postgres and Valkey.

env.PENPOT_PUBLIC_URI: The URL Penpot is served at. Every service in the stack is told the same value; share links and the exporter both depend on it.
env.PENPOT_SECRET_KEY: Signs sessions and the tokens the exporter authenticates with. The backend and the exporter must carry the same value.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres.

plausible.description: Privacy-friendly web analytics (Community Edition). Postgres holds app state, ClickHouse stores the event stream; migrations run automatically on boot.

env.BASE_URL: Public URL the dashboard is served from.
env.SECRET_KEY_BASE: Phoenix secret key base. At least 64 bytes.
env.TOTP_VAULT_KEY: Key that encrypts 2FA/TOTP secrets at rest (required since v3). Must be 32 bytes.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the postgres superuser.

pocket-id.description: OIDC provider built around passkeys, so there are no passwords to store or reset. Small enough to put in front of internal tools without running a full identity platform.

env.APP_URL: Public base URL. Issued tokens and OIDC discovery are built from it.

pocketbase.description: Backend in a single file: SQLite database, auth, file storage and a realtime API, with an admin UI. Everything persists to one named volume; no external database to run.

postiz.description: Schedule and publish to X, LinkedIn, Instagram, Mastodon, Discord and a dozen more from one calendar, with per-channel previews and an AI-assisted editor. Scheduling runs on a bundled Temporal server, so queued posts survive a restart.

env.POSTIZ_URL: The public URL you open Postiz at, scheme included. Every social account's OAuth callback and every uploaded image URL is built from it, so changing it later breaks both.
env.JWT_SECRET: Signs the session tokens. Rotating it signs everyone out; anything holding it can mint a session, so it never leaves the server.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres. It carries Postiz's own schema and the two databases Temporal creates for workflow state.

prestashop.description: A full storefront and back office: catalogue, checkout, taxes, shipping and a theme system, backed by MySQL.

env.PRESTASHOP_DOMAIN: The hostname the shop runs on, without a scheme. PrestaShop stores it and builds every absolute URL from it.
env.ADMIN_EMAIL: Email for the back-office account created during the automatic install.
env.ADMIN_PASSWORD: Password for that back-office account. PrestaShop requires at least eight characters.

qdrant.description: Vector database for semantic search and retrieval, with payload filtering and on-disk storage. REST on 6333, gRPC on 6334.

env.QDRANT_API_KEY: Bearer token required on every request. Qdrant ships with no authentication and its dashboard is a full read/write client, so an exposed instance without this key is an open database.

rabbitmq.description: Reliable message broker speaking AMQP (and more). Ships the management image so the web UI is available on 15672 alongside the AMQP port 5672; state persists to a named volume.

env.RABBITMQ_PASSWORD: Password for the default broker user.

rustfs.description: High-performance, S3-compatible object storage written in Rust: a MinIO alternative. S3 API on 9000; the web console is on 9001 at /rustfs/console. Objects persist to a named volume.

env.RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY: Root access key (S3 access key ID).
env.RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY: Root secret key (S3 secret access key).

soketi.description: Pusher-compatible websocket server. Keep the Pusher client SDKs and point them here instead. Drop-in realtime for Laravel Echo, Rails and anything speaking the protocol.

env.SOKETI_APP_KEY: Public app key clients connect with.
env.SOKETI_APP_SECRET: Server-side secret used to sign channel authorization.

stirling-pdf.description: A local toolbox of about fifty PDF operations — merge, split, OCR, sign, convert, redact — that runs entirely on your own server, so documents never leave it.

temporal.description: Durable workflow engine. Long-running processes survive crashes, deploys and retries because state lives in the server, not your process. Ships with the web UI.

env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres holding workflow history.

tooljet.description: Build internal tools visually against your own databases, APIs and cloud services, with a query builder and a component library.

env.TOOLJET_HOST: The full URL ToolJet is served at, scheme included. It is used as the origin for auth callbacks and embedded apps.
env.LOCKBOX_MASTER_KEY: Encrypts stored datasource credentials. Must be 32 bytes of hex.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres.

twenty.description: Open-source CRM: a modern, keyboard-first alternative to Salesforce. App and background worker share a bundled Postgres and Redis; uploads persist to a named volume.

env.SERVER_URL: Public URL Twenty is served from. Used for the API base and frontend links.
env.APP_SECRET: Secret used to sign sessions and tokens.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Superuser password for the bundled Postgres.

typesense.description: Typo-tolerant search engine tuned for instant results, with faceting and geo search, from a single binary and one data directory.

env.TYPESENSE_API_KEY: The admin key. It can create collections and scoped search-only keys, so keep it server-side and never ship it to a browser.

umami.description: Simple, fast, privacy-focused website analytics. One Node service over Postgres; the tracking script is served from the app itself.

env.APP_SECRET: Secret used to hash session tokens.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the umami Postgres user.

unleash.description: Feature-flag service with gradual rollouts, targeting rules and per-environment toggles. SDK-driven, so flags evaluate in your app rather than over the network per request.

env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres that stores flags and strategies.

uptime-kuma.description: Self-hosted uptime monitoring with status pages and notifications. Single service, zero required configuration. The first visit creates the admin user.

valkey.description: The community fork of Redis, for caching, queues and pub/sub. Append-only persistence is on, so a restart does not lose the dataset.

env.VALKEY_PASSWORD: Password clients authenticate with. Set this in the connecting application's Redis URL as well.

vaultwarden.description: Lightweight Bitwarden-compatible password server in Rust. Works with the official Bitwarden apps and browser extensions; data persists to a named volume.

env.DOMAIN: Public URL the vault is served from. Required for WebAuthn and the apps.

verdaccio.description: Private npm registry that proxies and caches the public one. Publish internal packages without paying for a private scope, and keep installing when npmjs is down.

vikunja.description: Task and project management with list, gantt, table and kanban views over the same data. Postgres-backed, with file attachments on their own volume.

env.VIKUNJA_URL: The URL the frontend is served at. Vikunja's API returns absolute links built from it.
env.VIKUNJA_JWT_SECRET: Signs the API tokens. Changing it signs every client out.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres.

wikijs.description: A modern wiki with Markdown and visual editors, Git-backed storage options and granular permissions. Everything else is configured through the setup wizard on first visit.

env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres.

windmill.description: Turn scripts in Python, TypeScript, Go, Bash or SQL into shared UIs, APIs and scheduled jobs. The server and the worker run the same image with different roles, so add workers to add throughput.

env.WINDMILL_BASE_URL: The URL Windmill is served at. Generated webhook and app URLs are built from it.
env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled Postgres, which is both the database and the job queue.

wordpress.description: The most-deployed CMS there is: themes, plugins and a familiar admin. Bundled MariaDB; the whole site directory persists to a named volume so plugins survive redeploys.

env.MYSQL_PASSWORD: Password for the bundled MariaDB user WordPress connects as.
env.MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: Root password for the bundled MariaDB.

templates.noRequiredVars: No required variables. This template deploys with safe defaults.
templates.noMatchHint: {{count}} match in other categories — {{category}} is what's excluding them.
templates.noMatchHintPlain: Try a different term, or browse a category from the rail.

compose.buildUnsupportedBefore: {{services}} build from source, which isn't supported yet. Use a prebuilt
compose.dialogServiceBefore: Pick what you want to launch. Otterdeploy can build app code, pull images, import compose stacks, or provision a database
compose.dialogTemplateAfter: . Nothing deploys until you apply the staged change.
compose.exposeHint: Click a port to expose it on a public domain.
compose.gitBlurbAfter: context, then deploys the whole stack. Track progress on the graph.
compose.gitBlurbBefore: Clones the repo, builds each service with a
compose.varsNoRefs: Set any variables this stack needs before it deploys.
compose.varsRequiredBanner: Fill in the fields flagged in red: they're required and still empty. Secrets are already generated; what's left is usually a URL or name only you know.
compose.varsShared: A red marker flags a required value that's still empty; click the eye to reveal or edit a secret. Saved as project variables.
compose.varsWithRefs: The compose file references these: secrets are auto-generated, defaults pre-filled.
compose.domainHelp: Where this stack will be reachable. Pre-filled with the address it would get anyway — change it to publish on your own hostname.

edgeLogs.wrapHint: Wrap long values in expanded rows instead of truncating
edgeLogs.bannedIp: This IP has an active CrowdSec ban: new requests are rejected at the edge.
edgeLogs.eventsEmpty: No edge events in this window. Certificate activity and upstream errors for your domains appear here.
edgeLogs.eventsSinkOff: Edge event collection is off on this install (EDGE_LOG_SINK is unset), so nothing can appear here — Caddy's certificate and upstream logs are going to the edge container's own output instead.

variables.duplicateNote: Duplicate key: another row is also named {{key}}. Rename or delete one to save.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where this service builds from. Pushing to its branch deploys it.
source.installationHint: Which connected account owns the repo.
source.branchHint: Pushes here deploy. Empty = repo default.
source.imageTargetHint: Fully-qualified, no tag. Empty = local build. Credential matched by host.
source.prPreviewsHint: Rebuild this service into an isolated preview environment for every pull request.
source.registryUnmatched: No registry credential for {{host}}. Add one in Registries or clear this.

resources.stackNoServicesGit: Services appear once the stack is built from the repo.
resources.stackNoServicesInline: This stack's compose file declares no services.
resources.stackFromRepo: This stack builds from a repository. The compose file lives in the repo and is resolved at build time.
resources.deleteStackBlurb: Removes every service in this stack from swarm, its routes, and the resource record. This can't be undone.
resources.deleteStackDescription: All {{n}} of its services are removed from swarm along with their routes and the resource record. This can't be undone.
resources.variablesStaged: Variables staged. Review and apply the pending changes.
resources.variablesSavedRedeploy: Variables saved. They take effect on the next redeploy
resources.publicAccessDescription: Off keeps the DB on the internal network only. On wires the Caddy layer-4 proxy and exposes the public hostname to the open internet.
resources.willBeExposedAfterDeploy: Will be exposed on the public internet after deploy
resources.publicAccessStaged: Public access staged. Deploy to apply

domains.dnsHintGenerated: This host doesn't resolve to this server yet. Point it here with the A record below (a wildcard on the base domain covers every generated host), then Recheck.
domains.dnsHintCustom: Add the ownership TXT record and point the host at this server, then Recheck. The route stays disabled until ownership is verified.
domains.sslipNote: Temporary address with a self-signed certificate, so browsers will warn. Add a domain of your own for a trusted URL.
domains.certSelfSignedHint: Serving a self-signed certificate — browsers will reject it. Run Recheck DNS once this host resolves to this server.
domains.certSelfSignedProxiedHint: Cloudflare serves a trusted certificate to visitors, but the origin here is self-signed. Keep Cloudflare SSL mode on Full (not Full strict), or grey-cloud the record briefly so a real certificate can issue.

backups.downloadSub: Fetch the decrypted archive to your machine. Nothing on the source changes.
backups.inPlaceSubVolume: Replaces the volume's contents with this archive. Refused while any container mounts it. Requires typed-name confirmation.
backups.inPlaceSubDatabase: Overwrites the current source with this snapshot. Requires typed-name confirmation.
backups.intoSub: Seeds a different database from this snapshot. That database's contents are overwritten, not this one's; the typed confirmation names the target.

vault.title: Secret providers
vault.description: Pull env-var values from an external secret manager at deploy time instead of storing them here.
vault.emptyDescription: Connect HashiCorp Vault, OpenBao, Infisical or Doppler and reference their secrets from any service's variables without copying values into otterdeploy.
vault.syntaxBefore: Reference a secret from any variable value as
vault.syntaxAfter: (fetched from the provider on every deploy, never stored here).
vault.dialogDescriptionBefore: Reference its secrets from any env var as
vault.dialogDescriptionAfter: . Values are fetched at deploy time and never stored here.
vault.credentialHintEdit: Leave blank to keep the stored credential.
vault.providerAdded: Provider added. Run a connection test to verify it
vault.removeConfirmAfter: will fail to resolve on its next deploy. The provider's own secrets are not touched.

fields.dopplerProjectHint: Only needed when the service token isn't scoped to one config.

refPicker.filterPlaceholder: Filter database, service or shared variables
refPicker.noRefs: No references defined yet in this project

variables.replacesIn: Replaces every variable in {{targets}}, atomic per environment.

routeAccess.title: Access
routeAccess.wallOn: Org members sign in automatically. Grant outside access with a guest invite, an access PIN, a shareable link, or a CI bypass token.
routeAccess.wallOff: The wall is off, so this deployment is public and these methods are not enforced. Turn on Protection to apply them.

guests.title: Guests
guests.hint: Invite people by email. They get a one-time code to sign in, no account, for the session length you pick.

pin.title: Access PIN
pin.hint: One shared numeric code (4–8 digits) anyone can enter on the wall. Rotating or removing it signs every PIN session out.

link.title: Shareable link
link.hint: A no-login URL anyone can open until it expires.

token.title: CI bypass token
token.hint: Send as the x-otter-bypass request header to skip the wall in automation.

collection.offBody: No access logs are reaching this install, so nothing is being recorded. This is not an empty window — no window would have data. Set this variable on the server (the production compose file already does) and restart it to start collecting.
collection.stalledTitle: Collection is configured but not running
collection.stalledBody: The sink is set, but the analytics rollup refused to start — it does that deliberately when its day-row seed fails, rather than risk overwriting earlier totals. Check the server log for this key; the next restart retries.
collection.noHostsBody: Collection is running. Analytics starts recording as soon as a service is exposed on a domain.
collection.quiet: Collecting. No requests in this window yet.
collection.geoOff: GeoIP isn't configured on this install, so visitor countries can't be resolved and the map stays empty.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.descriptionProject: Visitors, pages and sources for {{project}}, straight from the tracker.
analytics.descriptionInstall: Visitors, pages and sources for every tracked site on this install.
analytics.descriptionOrg: Visitors, pages and sources across your organization's tracked sites.

range.pickDays: Pick a start and end day.

filters.valuePlaceholder: Type a value or pick one below

overview.noSeries: The chart shows visitors — {{metric}} is a period total and has no time series.
overview.goalsEmpty: No goals yet. Mark an event as a conversion to track it here.
overview.nobodyNow: Nobody on the site right now.
overview.errorBody: The overview query failed. It retries automatically on the next refresh.
overview.footerSource: pageviews & visitors from the tracker; requests & latency live under Traffic
overview.nudgeNoSite: Web analytics isn't set up for {{project}} yet.
overview.nudgeWaiting: Waiting for the first pageview from {{project}}.
overview.nudgeWaitingAny: Sites are set up, but no pageview has arrived yet.
overview.nudgeNone: Web analytics isn't set up for any project yet.
overview.noDataHint: Nothing matched this dimension in the selected range and filters.

realtime.nobody: Nobody on the site right now.
realtime.noOnlineBody: Visitors active in the last five minutes appear here.
realtime.noRecent: No sessions in the last 24 hours.
realtime.trailDescription: Today's sessions for this visitor. Identities rotate daily and are never stored.
realtime.trailEmpty: No trail for this visitor today.

traffic.visitorDaysHelp: Distinct visitors summed per UTC day (bots excluded). Per-day counts can't be merged into unique visitors for the whole window.
traffic.latencyHelp: p95 over the window, from merged latency histograms.
traffic.errorBody: The traffic query failed. It retries automatically on the next refresh.
traffic.approximate: Visitor counts in this window are approximate: the visitor set was rebuilt after a restart or hit its memory cap, so some days undercount or double-count returning visitors.
traffic.breakdownDays_one: Breakdowns (statuses, paths, countries, devices) are per UTC day and cover the {{count}} calendar day touching this window.
traffic.breakdownDays_other: Breakdowns (statuses, paths, countries, devices) are per UTC day and cover the {{count}} calendar days touching this window.

events.emptyBody: Send one from your site and it appears here, ready to be named and marked as a conversion.
events.name: Name

funnels.description: Define a sequence of pages and events and see where visitors drop off between steps.

setup.pickProject: Choose a project to set up
setup.pickProjectBody: Each project gets its own tracking key and snippet.
setup.ensureFailed: Couldn't create the tracking site for this project.
setup.installationDesc: Paste this snippet into {{project}}'s HTML, just before </head>.
setup.worksWith: Works with any framework; SPA route changes are tracked automatically.
setup.docTrack: Record a custom event with optional properties.
setup.docIdentify: Attach a hashed user id to the visitor's sessions.
setup.docAttr: Record an event when the element is clicked.
setup.docIgnore: Add this id to any element whose clicks must be ignored.
setup.hostsDesc: Events are only accepted from these hosts; everything else is rejected at collect.
setup.allowedHostsDesc: Every public domain routed to this project, kept in sync automatically.
setup.noHosts: No domains routed to this project yet.
setup.extraHostsDesc: Hosts served elsewhere (a static site, a marketing page) that should report here.
setup.privacyDesc: Cookieless by design; these switches decide when the tracker stays silent.
setup.respectDntDesc: Skip visitors whose browser sends DNT or Global Privacy Control.
setup.requireConsentDesc: Stay silent until your site calls otter.consent().
setup.excludePathsDesc: One glob per line. Matching pageviews are dropped at collect.
setup.healthDesc: Collector counters since the server last started. They reset on restart.

stat.botsDesc: Dropped by the user-agent bot list.
stat.rejectedHostDesc: Sent from a host not in the list above.

setup.dangerDesc: Actions that break the snippet already on your site.
setup.rotateKeyDesc: Mints a new key. The snippet on your site stops working until you replace it.
setup.rotateConfirmBody: The old snippet stops being accepted within a minute. Paste the new snippet to keep collecting.
